title: Thread Pool: Worker Staffing Office
concept: Creating a new thread every time is expensive. There is a need for a ‘manpower office’ that has workers on standby in advance and only gives them work.

steps.title: Import the required classes
steps.explanation:
**`import java.util.concurrent.*;`**

Prefetch for use by `ExecutorService` and friends that manage the thread pool.

steps.title: Human Resources Office (ThreadPool) opened
steps.explanation:
**`Executors.newFixedThreadPool(3)`**

We open an office with three full-time workers.
Now, when work comes in, these three people take turns handling it.
There is no cost of finding a new part-time worker (creating a thread) every time.

**Similar**: It is like having three drivers waiting at the ‘delivery agency office’.
Once an order (task) is received, the waiting driver will depart immediately.

steps.title: Submit your first job
steps.explanation:
Submit the first task (lambda function) to the thread pool via `execute()`.
One of the waiting threads takes over this task and executes it.

steps.title: Submit second job
steps.explanation:
Then submit the second task.
Another waiting thread immediately takes over this task and executes it.
If all threads are working, the task will be waiting in the queue.

steps.title: Thread pool exit
steps.explanation:
Shut down the thread pool by calling `shutdown()`.
It no longer accepts new work, and threads are safely terminated when all work currently in progress is completed.
If you forget this call, your program will never end.

memoryState.note: Once all tasks finish, the threads are safely destroyed.

quiz.question: Which of the following is not a main reason for using a thread pool?
options: Reduce the cost of creating and deleting threads
Responding to a sudden surge in work
Speeds up the shutdown of the entire program
Efficient use of resources (memory and CPU)
quiz.explanation:
Rather, if you do not close the thread pool properly, the process may remain alive without being terminated.
It is not directly related to shutdown speed.

misconceptions.wrong: The more threads there are, the faster it is.
misconceptions.correct: no! If there are too many threads than the number of CPUs, it becomes slower because there is a fight to see who will go first (Context Switch) instead of doing any work.
misconceptions.why: The thread pool is used to adjust the number of workers appropriate to system specifications.

keyTakeaway: ExecutorService is the core of modern Java concurrent programming. Use a pool rather than creating threads yourself!
